About ProFound Therapeutics

ProFound™ Therapeutics is a biotechnology company discovering novel proteins across the expanded human proteome to unlock first-in-class medicines and transformative drug targets. The company’s proprietary ProFoundry™ Platform integrates state-of-the-art protein detection, validation, and computational technologies to systematically identify and characterize previously inaccessible proteins and validate their therapeutic potential. This approach has generated a rapidly expanding portfolio of novel targets and drug discovery programs advancing toward the clinic, enabled by strategic collaborations with leading pharmaceutical partners. Together, these efforts support the development of breakthrough treatments across a broad range of disease areas.

The company is now poised to define the disease-relevant function of these proteins at scale using advanced proteomics technologies, high throughput experimental biology, and causal agentic AI, enabling rapid identification and characterization of the most promising protein drugs and drug targets.

Founded by Flagship Pioneering, ProFound works with pharmaceutical partners including Novartis, Pfizer and GSK, and with the Gates Foundation, which has committed up to $35 million to a ProFoundprogram focused on preeclampsia.

About Flagship Pioneering

ProFound Therapeutics was founded by Flagship Pioneering's venture creation engine that invents and builds platform companies, each with the potential for multiple products that transform human health or sustainability. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated and fostered more than 100 scientific ventures, resulting in more than $90 billion in aggregate value. Many of the company’s Flagship has founded have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture. Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies and has been twice named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies. Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program

Welcome to Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program for the cohort dreaming big and taking courageous leaps. You'll join fellow peers across our ecosystem of companies and learning firsthand how we build first-in-category companies. You’ll have access to enrichment sessions, a dedicated professional development track, and a mentor that help guide you toward your next step. Position Summary

ProFound’s AI/ML team builds SAGE, an internal multi-agent LLM platform that helps our scientists reason over knowledge graphs, biological databases and the scientific literature. SAGE is a central part of how ProFound applies agentic AI to understand novel proteins and accelerate drug discovery.

As an AI/ML Engineering Co-Op, you will help extend what SAGE can do and make sure it performs reliably. You will own real features from design through deployment, working closely with our ML engineers and with the scientists who use SAGE every day. The Co-Op is designed to complement your academic training with hands-on experience building and operating a production AI system in an industry drug discovery setting.

Scope

- Agent tools and integrations, including external data sources, MCP servers and user-uploaded documents

- User experience and collaboration features in the SAGE chat interface

- LLM evaluation and benchmarking (answer quality, accuracy and hallucination rate)

- Monitoring of usage, performance and cost, and quality checks in CI/CD

Key Responsibilities

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following.

- Tools and capabilities

- Design, build and ship new SAGE tools that connect the agent to external data sources, APIs and MCP servers.

- Extend SAGE’s ability to ingest and reason over documents that users upload, including parsing, chunking and retrieval.

- Contribute to agent orchestration and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) components that work across knowledge graphs, biological databases and the scientific literature.

- User experience

- Build features that make the SAGE chat interface easier to use and collaborate in (e.g., sharing conversations, displaying sources and citations).

- Gather feedback directly from scientists and turn it into practical, prioritized improvements.

- Evaluation and quality

- Develop evaluation and benchmarking pipelines that measure SAGE’s answer quality, accuracy and hallucination rate.

- Help build and curate benchmark datasets with input from scientists, using automated (e.g., LLM-as-judge) and human-review approaches.

- Help integrate automated quality checks and regression tests into our CI/CD pipeline.

- Monitoring and engineering practice

- Build monitoring for SAGE usage, performance, reliability and LLM cost.

- Write clean, tested and documented code, and take part in code reviews.

- Present progress and results to the AI/ML team and scientific stakeholders, including a final co-op presentation.

What Success Looks Like by the End of the Co-Op

- At least one new SAGE capability designed, built and deployed to production, and in use by scientists.

- An evaluation and benchmarking pipeline running regularly, giving the team a clear baseline for answer quality and hallucination rate.

- Better visibility into SAGE usage, performance and cost.

- Well-documented work that the team can maintain and build on after the co-op ends.

Qualifications

Required

- Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related field, and available for a full-time, 4–6 month co-op term.

- Strong Python skills.

- Hands-on experience building with LLMs (e.g., LLM APIs, RAG, agents, or MCP) through coursework, projects, or prior internships

- Familiarity with Git and software engineering best practices, such as testing, code review and documentation.

- Curious and self-driven, with the ability to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical colleagues.

Preferred

- Experience with web or backend development (e.g., FastAPI, React or TypeScript).

- Experience with LLM evaluation frameworks or observability and tracing tools.

- Exposure to knowledge graphs, vector databases, or scientific and biological data sources.

- Familiarity with cloud environments (e.g., AWS), containers (e.g., Docker) and CI/CD tooling (e.g., GitHub Actions).

- Prior internship or co-op experience in software or ML engineering.

- Interest in biology or drug discovery; no biology background required.

Why Join Us?

You’ll work on a production AI platform used by real scientists. You’ll own projects end to end, with mentorship from experienced ML engineers, and contribute to the discovery of new medicines.

What We Offer

- Build alongside founders. You’ll work inside the same hypothesis-driven process Flagship uses to conceive and launch first-in-category companies.

About Base

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role

At Base, we're building BaseOS: the operating system that runs the modern power company. It's the firmware on batteries in more than 15,000 homes nationally, the algorithms that balance power in real-time energy markets, the internal tools that deploy and operate a fleet installing roughly 150 batteries a day, and the product members use to see and control their energy.

As a software engineering intern, you'll ship real code that runs in production on systems that keep power flowing to real homes. You'll work on problems that touch the whole company: balancing electrons in milliseconds, scaling operations into new markets, and automating things most utilities still do by hand.

This is one of the few places where every line of code has real consequences, in homes, on the grid, and in how Base grows.

What You'll Do

- Build production systems. Design, build, and deploy production-grade software across the stack, from embedded firmware to backend infrastructure to member-facing products.

- Ship under real constraints. Write code that runs under real-world conditions, where failures have physical consequences. Reliability isn't an afterthought, it's the job.

- Scale Base's operations. Contribute to the internal tools that let us expand into new markets, handle paperwork and deployment complexity, and orchestrate field operations at scale.

- Work across domains. Partner with hardware, deployment, and operations teams to solve problems that span software and the physical world.

What You'll Bring

- A strong foundation in software engineering fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, systems design.

- Demonstrated ability to build and ship working software, through side projects, coursework, or prior internships.

- A clear, concise communicator who works well in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

- A builder's mindset: curious, self-directed, drawn to problems that actually matter.

Areas You Can Work In

(Please indicate your area(s) of interest when applying)

- Member software. Everything close to the member: top-of-funnel marketing and growth, onboarding, and the support members get once they've signed up for Base, including bill pay, live telemetry, grid status, and the systems that keep answering correctly through retries, outages, and partial failures.

- Factory software. The platform that tracks everything moving in and out of Base's factory: parts, vendors, procurement, receiving, and inventory, plus the tools that connect what happens on the floor to what shows up in our financial systems. - Dig into high-impact areas including experience/appointment creation, ticket transfers, co-hosting, and beyond

- Identify gaps, edge cases, and failure states with a structured, user-centered lens

- Propose and prioritize improvements, then partner with engineering and design to execute them

- Where scope allows, own new feature work end-to-end — from problem definition and spec to launch

- Define and drive analytics for recently launched features — identify what to measure, work with engineering to ensure tracking is in place, and synthesize early signal into actionable takeaways

- Own a competitive analysis workstream for growth-adjacent features (referrals, PLG, network effects) and synthesize findings into clear product recommendations

- Data analysis and synthesis to support roadmap decisions

- Where relevant, contribute to 0-to-1 discovery work for upcoming features — user research synthesis, problem framing, or lightweight spec writing

- Develop and apply a bug priority rubric for revenue-generating and operations-critical workflows

- Maintain backlog health: consolidate duplicates, triage stale items, and ensure active issues have the right context, owners, and priorities
